examples.ko: 어제 운동을 너무 많이 해서 다리가 욱신거려요.
examples.en: I exercised too much yesterday, so my legs are throbbing.

examples.ko: 이가 계속 욱신거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My tooth kept throbbing, so I couldn't sleep.
Does the knee you fell on still throb?

examples.ko: 비가 오려고 하면 어깨가 욱신거리기 시작해요.
examples.en: When it's about to rain, my shoulder starts to ache.

examples.ko: 손가락이 욱신거리는데 병원에 가 봐야 할까요?
examples.en: My finger is throbbing. Should I go to the hospital?

examples.ko: 약을 먹었더니 욱신거리던 머리가 좀 나아졌어요.
examples.en: After I took medicine, my throbbing head got a bit better.

explain: 그냥 '아프다'보다 맥박 치듯 계속 쑤시는 느낌이에요. 다치거나 부딪친 곳, 근육통, 치통에 자주 써요. 보통 '다리가 욱신거려요'처럼 아픈 부위를 주어로 말해요.
explain_en: It is more specific than plain '아프다': a dull pain that keeps pulsing. It is often used for injuries, muscle soreness and toothaches. You usually make the sore body part the subject, as in '다리가 욱신거려요'.

examples.en: The bag was small, but I crammed the clothes in anyway.
I was in a hurry, so I stuffed bread into my mouth and ran out.

examples.ko: 짐을 다 욱여넣어도 가방이 안 닫혀요.
examples.en: Even if I cram all the stuff in, the bag won't close.
Don't cram the papers into the drawer; organize them.
Lunch break was short, so I shoveled my food down.

examples.ko: 좁은 트렁크에 짐을 욱여넣느라 땀이 났어요.
examples.en: I broke a sweat cramming the luggage into the small trunk.

explain: '넣다'와 달리 좁은 곳에 억지로 밀어 넣는 느낌이 강해요. 짐이나 옷뿐 아니라 음식을 입에 급하게 넣을 때도 써요. 말할 때는 '쑤셔 넣다'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 그쪽이 좀 더 거칠게 들려요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '넣다', it carries a strong sense of forcing things into a tight space. It works for luggage and clothes, and also for hurriedly stuffing food into your mouth. In speech '쑤셔 넣다' is similar, but it sounds a bit rougher.

examples.ko: 선거 운동원들이 거리에서 명함을 나눠 줘요.
examples.en: Campaign workers are handing out business cards on the street.

examples.ko: 저는 이번 선거 때 운동원으로 일했어요.
examples.en: I worked as a campaigner in this election.
A campaigner came all the way to my door to say hello.

examples.ko: 그 후보는 운동원을 백 명 넘게 모았어요.
examples.en: That candidate gathered more than a hundred campaign workers.

examples.ko: 운동원들은 모두 파란 점퍼를 입고 있었어요.
examples.en: The campaign workers were all wearing blue jackets.

examples.ko: 아르바이트로 선거 운동원을 구한다는 광고를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw an ad looking for election campaign workers for a part-time job.

explain: 거의 '선거 운동원'처럼 선거 이야기에서 나와요. 운동하는 사람을 뜻하는 '운동선수'와 헷갈리지 않게 조심하세요. 뉴스나 선거철 대화에서 자주 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It almost always appears as '선거 운동원' in talk about elections. Be careful not to confuse it with '운동선수', an athlete. You will hear it in the news and during election season.

examples.ko: 그는 모든 일이 정해져 있다는 운명론을 믿어요.
examples.en: He believes in fatalism, that everything is already decided.

examples.ko: 운명론에 빠지면 노력을 안 하게 될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you fall into fatalism, you might stop making an effort.

examples.ko: 저는 운명론보다 노력이 더 중요하다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think effort matters more than fatalism.
This movie deals with a fatalistic story.

examples.ko: 친구는 운명론자라서 다 이유가 있다고 자주 말해요.
examples.en: My friend is a fatalist, so he often says everything happens for a reason.

examples.ko: 운명론은 철학 수업에서 자주 나오는 주제예요.
examples.en: Fatalism is a common topic in philosophy class.

explain: 사람을 말할 때는 '운명론자', 성격이나 분위기를 말할 때는 '운명론적'으로 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '팔자'라는 말로 비슷한 생각을 표현하기도 해요. 주로 철학·영화·토론처럼 생각을 이야기하는 자리에서 나와요.
explain_en: For a person you say '운명론자', and for a mood or attitude you often say '운명론적'. In everyday talk people may express a similar idea with the word '팔자'. It mostly appears when discussing ideas, such as in philosophy, films and debates.

examples.en: These song lyrics are close to verse.
A novel is prose and a poem is verse.

examples.ko: 이 글은 운문으로 쓰여서 리듬이 느껴져요.
examples.en: This text is written in verse, so you can feel the rhythm.

examples.ko: 옛날 이야기를 운문 형식으로 바꿔 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried turning an old story into verse form.

examples.ko: 국어 시험에 운문과 산문을 구분하는 문제가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The Korean exam had a question about telling verse from prose.

examples.ko: 저는 산문보다 운문이 더 읽기 편해요.
examples.en: I find verse easier to read than prose.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '산문'이에요. 시나 노랫말처럼 리듬이 있는 글을 가리켜서 국어 수업과 시험에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '시'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '산문' (prose). It refers to writing with rhythm, such as poems and lyrics, and shows up a lot in Korean classes and exams. In daily conversation people often just say '시'.

examples.en: The delivery cost came out higher than the price of the furniture.

examples.ko: 이 가격에 운반비는 따로 내야 하나요?
examples.en: At this price, do I have to pay the transport fee separately?
It's a heavy item, so we charge extra for transport.
The owner even gave me a discount on the transport fee.

examples.ko: 산 위에 있는 집이라 운반비가 많이 붙어요.
examples.en: It's a house up on a mountain, so the transport fee adds up.
If you buy more than 50,000 won, transport is free.

explain: 가구나 큰 짐처럼 무겁고 큰 물건을 옮기는 비용에 자주 써요. 온라인 쇼핑 택배 이야기에서는 보통 '배송비'라고 말해요. 물건 값과 '따로' 내는지 묻는 상황에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is often used for the cost of moving heavy or large goods such as furniture. For online shopping parcels people usually say '배송비' instead. It comes up a lot when asking whether the fee is charged separately from the price.

en: transport industry; freight industry; transportation business

examples.en: My uncle has worked in the freight business for ten years.

examples.ko: 온라인 쇼핑이 늘면서 운송업이 점점 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: As online shopping grows, the transport industry keeps getting bigger.
The transport industry is greatly affected by fuel prices.
My father works in the transport industry.

examples.ko: 운송업 쪽으로 취업하려고 큰 면허를 땄어요.
examples.en: I got a large vehicle license to find a job in transport.
People in the transport business are busy from the early morning.

explain: 물건을 실어 나르는 일을 하는 사업을 크게 묶어 말할 때 써요. '택배업'처럼 더 구체적인 말도 있고, 운송업은 뉴스나 기사에서 큰 틀로 말할 때 자주 나와요. 일하는 곳을 말할 때는 '운송업을 하다', '운송업에 종사하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It is a broad term for the business of carrying goods. There are more specific words such as '택배업' (parcel delivery), while 운송업 often appears in news when talking about the industry as a whole. To describe someone's work, say '운송업을 하다' or '운송업에 종사하다'.

examples.ko: 새 팀에서는 제 운신의 폭이 좁아요.
examples.en: On my new team, my room to maneuver is narrow.
I hurt my back, so even moving around is hard.
It's a small room, so there's no space to move around.
There were so many people that it was hard to move.

examples.ko: 비자 문제 때문에 운신에 제약이 많아요.
examples.en: Because of my visa situation, I have many limits on what I can do.
I'm so aware of people's eyes that I can't move freely.

explain: 혼자 쓰기보다 '운신의 폭', '운신이 어렵다'처럼 굳은 모양으로 많이 나와요. 몸을 움직이는 것뿐 아니라 어떤 일을 자유롭게 할 수 있는 범위를 말할 때도 써요. 말투가 딱딱해서 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 계약 때문에 제 운신의 폭이 좁아졌어요.
phrases.en: to have little freedom to act
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 아니라 상황 때문에 할 수 있는 일이 제한될 때 비유로 써요. 반대는 '운신의 폭이 넓다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when circumstances, not the body, limit what you can do. The opposite is '운신의 폭이 넓다'.

explain_en: It is rarely used alone and mostly appears in set forms such as '운신의 폭' and '운신이 어렵다'. It can mean physically moving, but also how freely you can act in a situation. The tone is stiff, so you see it more in news and writing.

examples.en: Thousands of people gathered in the square.
Fans are crowded in front of the stadium.

examples.ko: 가수를 보려고 운집한 사람들 때문에 길이 막혔어요.
examples.en: The road was blocked by the crowd gathered to see the singer.

examples.ko: 시청 앞에 시민들이 운집해서 행사를 구경했어요.
examples.en: Citizens crowded in front of City Hall and watched the event.
It's a big match where a huge crowd gathers.

examples.ko: 불꽃놀이를 보러 한강에 사람들이 운집할 거예요.
examples.en: People will crowd to the Han River to watch the fireworks.

explain: '모이다'와 달리 아주 많은 사람이 한곳에 몰릴 때만 써요. 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 나오는 딱딱한 말이라 일상 대화에서는 '모이다', '몰리다'를 더 많이 말해요. 보통 '사람들이 운집하다'처럼 사람이 주어예요.
explain_en: Unlike '모이다', it is used only when a very large crowd packs into one place. It is a stiff word common in news, so in daily talk people more often say '모이다' or '몰리다'. The subject is usually people, as in '사람들이 운집하다'.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날의 카페는 운치가 있어요.
examples.en: A cafe on a rainy day has a lovely atmosphere.

examples.ko: 한옥 마당에 앉아 있으니 운치 있네요.
examples.en: Sitting in the hanok yard is so charming.

examples.ko: 이 골목은 운치는 있지만 좀 불편해요.
examples.en: This alley has charm, but it's a bit inconvenient.
The old tile-roofed house adds to the charm.
The new building is neat, but it has no charm.

examples.ko: 운치 없게 갑자기 불을 켜면 어떡해요?
examples.en: How could you spoil the mood by suddenly turning on the light?

explain: '분위기'는 좋고 나쁨 모두에 쓰지만, 운치는 조용하고 멋스러운 정취를 칭찬할 때 써요. 대부분 '운치가 있다/없다' 모양으로 말해요. 비 오는 날, 한옥, 오래된 골목처럼 차분한 장면에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '분위기' can be good or bad, but 운치 is used to praise a quiet, tasteful charm. It mostly appears as '운치가 있다/없다'. It suits calm scenes such as rainy days, hanok houses and old alleys.

examples.ko: 우리는 벽을 짙은 색깔로 울긋불긋 꾸몄어요.
examples.en: We decorated the wall in deep colors, all colorful.
When autumn came, the mountains turned a riot of colors.
The children gathered, wearing colorful hanbok.
The flowers in the flower bed are blooming in many colors.
Colorful fruit is piled up in the market.

examples.ko: 설날 거리에 울긋불긋 등이 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: Colorful lanterns are hanging on the streets for the New Year.

explain: 여러 가지 진한 색이 섞여 화려하게 보이는 모습이에요. 단풍, 꽃, 옷, 장식처럼 눈에 확 들어오는 것에 많이 써요. '알록달록'도 비슷한 말로 쓰여요.
explain_en: It describes many strong colors mixed together and looking gorgeous. It is often used for autumn leaves, flowers, clothes and decorations that catch the eye. '알록달록' is a similar word.

examples.ko: 우리는 벽을 짙은 색깔로 울긋불긋하게 꾸몄어요.
examples.en: We decorated the wall in deep colors, making it colorful.
The living room is so colorful that my eyes feel dizzy.
The mountain is a blaze of color with the autumn leaves.

examples.ko: 울긋불긋한 옷을 입으니 눈에 확 띄어요.
examples.en: Wearing such colorful clothes really makes you stand out.
The colorful leaves have all fallen.

examples.ko: 산이 가장 울긋불긋할 때 사진을 찍어요.
examples.en: Let's take photos when the mountain is at its most colorful.

explain: 색이 여러 가지로 섞여 화려할 때 써요. '울긋불긋한 옷', '울긋불긋하게 꾸미다'처럼 뒤에 오는 말에 맞춰 활용해요. 너무 요란해서 정신없다는 느낌으로 말할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when many colors mix into a gaudy, bright look. Conjugate it to fit what follows, as in '울긋불긋한 옷' or '울긋불긋하게 꾸미다'. It can also carry a sense of being so flashy it feels busy.

examples.ko: 발표 전에 가슴이 울렁여서 물을 마셨어요.
examples.en: My heart was fluttering before the presentation, so I drank some water.
As soon as I got on the boat, my stomach started to heave.
My heart flutters when I see the person I like.
I could feel the boat rolling on the waves.

examples.ko: 차 안에서 책을 읽었더니 속이 울렁였어요.
examples.en: I read a book in the car, and my stomach felt queasy.

examples.ko: 합격 소식에 가슴이 울렁이던 순간이 아직 기억나요.
examples.en: I still remember the moment my heart fluttered at the news that I passed.

explain: 가슴에 쓰면 설렘이나 긴장으로 두근거리는 느낌이고, 속에 쓰면 멀미처럼 메스꺼운 느낌이에요. 어느 쪽인지는 '가슴이', '속이' 같은 앞말로 알 수 있어요. '울렁거리다'도 비슷하게 쓰여요.
explain_en: With '가슴' it means a fluttering heart from excitement or nerves, and with '속' it means a queasy, motion-sickness feeling. The word before it, '가슴이' or '속이', tells you which. '울렁거리다' is used in a similar way.

en: be close to tears; be on the verge of tears

examples.en: The child saw his mother and got teary.
My friend began her story on the verge of tears.

examples.ko: 목소리가 울먹거려서 무슨 일이 있는지 물어봤어요.
examples.en: Her voice was shaky with tears, so I asked what was wrong.
She said thank you in a voice choked with tears.

examples.ko: 혼나고 나서 울먹거리던 동생이 결국 울었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling, who was close to tears after being scolded, finally cried.
At the awards ceremony, he gave his speech with tears welling up.

explain: 완전히 우는 '울다'가 아니라 울음이 터지기 직전, 목소리나 표정에 울음이 섞인 상태예요. 그래서 '울먹거리는 목소리', '울먹거리며 말하다'처럼 말하는 모습과 자주 같이 나와요. 슬픔뿐 아니라 감동했을 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is not full crying like '울다' but the moment just before tears, when your voice or face is mixed with them. So it often pairs with speaking, as in '울먹거리는 목소리' and '울먹거리며 말하다'. It can come from sadness or from being moved.

examples.ko: 아이가 울며불며 장난감을 사 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: The child cried and wailed, begging me to buy a toy.

examples.ko: 동생은 울며불며 안 가겠다고 떼를 썼어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling bawled and insisted on not going.
On the day of parting, the family saw him off in tears.
Even though I clung to him in tears, it was no use this time.
He wept and wailed, begging for forgiveness.
I got a call from someone sobbing that they failed the exam.

explain: 소리 내어 울면서 야단을 피우는 모습이에요. 조용히 눈물만 흘릴 때가 아니라 크게 울고 호소하거나 떼쓸 때 써요. '울고불고'도 비슷하게 말해요.
explain_en: It describes crying loudly and making a scene. It is not for quietly shedding tears, but for bawling while pleading or throwing a fit. '울고불고' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: When the graduation ceremony ended, the classroom turned into a sea of tears.
At the film's last scene, the theater was a sea of tears.

examples.ko: 선생님의 편지를 읽자 반이 울음바다로 변했어요.
examples.en: When we read the teacher's letter, the class dissolved into tears.
The father's letter turned the wedding hall into a sea of tears.

examples.ko: 울음바다가 된 교실에서 선생님도 눈물을 닦았어요.
examples.en: In the classroom full of tears, even the teacher wiped her eyes.

examples.ko: 헤어지는 날은 모두가 울음바다 속에서 인사했어요.
examples.en: On the day we parted, everyone said goodbye amid a flood of tears.

explain: 여러 사람이 한꺼번에 울어서 온통 눈물인 분위기를 말해요. 보통 '~이/가 울음바다가 되다'로 쓰고, 한 사람이 우는 때는 쓰지 않아요. 졸업식, 이별, 감동적인 장면에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It describes a scene where many people cry at once and tears are everywhere. It usually appears as '~이/가 울음바다가 되다' and is not used when only one person cries. It is common for graduations, partings and moving scenes.

examples.en: The child suddenly burst into tears.
The moment I saw Mom's face, I burst out crying.

examples.ko: 동생은 울음보가 한번 터지면 잘 안 그쳐요.
examples.en: Once my younger sibling starts crying, it's hard to stop.
At my friend's comfort, I burst into the tears I had been holding back.

examples.ko: 울음보는 한 번 터지면 막기 어려워요.
examples.en: Once the tears start flowing, they are hard to stop.
My face turned red from holding back my tears.

explain: 울음이 가득 들어 있는 주머니처럼 보는 말이라 거의 '터지다', '터뜨리다'와 함께 써요. 아이나 감정이 북받친 사람이 갑자기 크게 울 때 잘 어울려요. 단독으로 말하기보다 굳은 짝말로 외워 두세요.

phrases.example: 시상식에서 그 선수는 결국 울음보를 터뜨렸어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참았던 울음을 한꺼번에 크게 쏟아낼 때 써요. 조용히 눈물이 나는 것과는 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when held-back crying comes out all at once and loudly, unlike quietly shedding tears.

explain_en: It treats crying as something stored in a pouch, so it almost always goes with '터지다' or '터뜨리다'. It suits a child or an emotional person suddenly crying hard. Learn it as a fixed collocation rather than on its own.

examples.en: The road is bumpy, so it's hard to walk.
I could see bulging muscles on his arm.
My facial skin has become bumpy, and I'm worried.
After the rain stopped, the dirt road is lumpy.
The trunk of an old tree looks knobby.
I fixed the bumpy wall so it's smooth.

explain: 표면이 평평하지 않고 군데군데 불거져 나온 모습이에요. 길, 근육, 피부, 나무껍질처럼 겉이 고르지 않은 것에 써요. 반대로 표면이 고를 때는 '매끈하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It describes a surface that is not flat and has bumps sticking out here and there. It is used for roads, muscles, skin and tree bark whose surface is uneven. The opposite, for an even surface, is '매끈하다'.

examples.en: After being treated unfairly, I was filled with pent-up anger.
I went to karaoke to let out the anger inside me.
After holding it in for so long, my anger built up.
My chest feels tight because of suppressed anger.
The boss couldn't hold back his anger and shouted.

examples.ko: 울화에 찬 얼굴로 그가 방에서 나왔어요.
examples.en: He came out of the room with a face full of rage.

explain: 바로 터지는 '화'와 달리 속에 참고 눌러서 쌓인 화를 말해요. '울화가 치밀다', '울화가 쌓이다', '울화를 풀다'처럼 짝말로 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '화가 나다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Unlike '화' that flares up right away, it means anger that has been held in and piled up inside. It often appears in collocations such as '울화가 치밀다', '울화가 쌓이다' and '울화를 풀다'. In daily talk people also just say '화가 나다'.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 기다렸는데 취소라니 울화통이 터져요.
examples.en: I waited all day and it's canceled? I'm furious.

examples.ko: 뉴스를 보다가 울화통이 터져서 TV를 껐어요.
examples.en: I got so angry watching the news that I turned off the TV.

examples.ko: 저 사람은 말을 들으면 울화통만 터져요.
examples.en: Listening to that person only makes my blood boil.
I drank cold water to calm my rage.
There are more infuriating things than I can count.
The unreasonable argument made me boil with anger, but I held back.

explain: '울화'를 속에서 끓는 통에 비유한 말이라 '터지다', '치밀다'와 자주 같이 써요. 화가 아주 많이 나서 참기 힘들 때 구어체로 말해요. 격식 있는 자리보다는 친구나 가족과의 대화에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 동생이 또 거짓말을 해서 울화통이 터질 뻔했어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참았던 화가 폭발하듯 아주 크게 화날 때 써요. 일상 대화에서 흔히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when anger you held in feels like it is exploding. It is common in everyday talk.

explain_en: It pictures '울화' as a pot boiling inside you, so it often goes with '터지다' or '치밀다'. It is a spoken word for anger so strong it is hard to bear. It suits chats with friends and family more than formal settings.

examples.ko: 산속에 낡은 움막이 한 채 있어요.
examples.en: There is one old hut in the mountains.

examples.ko: 옛날 사람들은 땅을 파고 움막을 지었어요.
examples.en: People long ago dug into the ground and built dugout huts.
I went into a nearby hut to get out of the rain.
I spent one night in the hut and it was freezing.
They lived in a house like a dugout hut.

examples.ko: 겨울이 되기 전에 움막을 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: We have to fix the hut before winter comes.

explain: 땅을 파거나 낮게 지어서 위를 덮은, 허술하고 임시로 쓰는 집이에요. 옛날 생활이나 산속의 초라한 집을 이야기할 때 나와요. 작고 소박한 집을 말하는 '오두막'과 비슷하지만, 움막은 더 허름하고 낮은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is a crude, temporary shelter dug into the ground or built low and covered over. It comes up when talking about life in the past or a shabby shelter in the mountains. It is similar to '오두막', a small simple cabin, but 움막 feels lower and more rundown.
